:::{#exm-Cox}
## Proportional Cox model
Consider the data set presented in @tbl-Survival_Data. We want to investigate the effect of `sex` and `age` on the survival time of lung cancer patients. A common approach is to use the Cox proportional hazards model.


:::{.panel-tabset}
## R
```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
# Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(survival)
library(survminer)

# Data
data_f <- survival::lung |>
    dplyr::select(-c(ph.ecog, ph.karno, pat.karno, meal.cal, wt.loss)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(sex = dplyr::if_else(sex == 1, "Male", "Female")) |>
    dplyr::mutate_at(.vars = c("inst", "status", "sex"), .funs = as.factor)

# Model
# * status == 2: event, status == 1: censored
cox_fit <- survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + sex, data_f, ties = "breslow")

## Model assumptions
survival::cox.zph(cox_fit) # Test if covariate HR changes over time

## Coefficients
broom::tidy(cox_fit)
```

## Python
```{python}
#| eval: false
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
# Packages
import pandas as pd
import lifelines
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Data
# Fetch survival::lung from the Rdatasets repository (no R needed)
lung = sm.datasets.get_rdataset("lung", "survival").data

data = (
    lung
    .loc[:, ["time", "status", "age", "sex"]]
    .assign(
        status=lambda d: (d["status"] == 2).astype(int),
        sex=lambda d: d["sex"].map({1: "Male", 2: "Female"}),
    )
    .dropna()
)

# Model
# * status == 1: event, status == 0: censored
cph = CoxPHFitter()
cph.fit(data, duration_col = 'time', event_col = 'status', formula = 'age + sex')

## Coefficients
cph.print_summary()
```
